stem: Let $n_1(x)=\frac{x^2-{=p*p}}{x^2-{=s}x+{=t}}$ and $n_2(x)=\frac{x^2+{=p}x}{x^2-{=q}x}$. The two fractions have the same simplest form but are not equal, because their domains differ. $n_1(x)=n_2(x)$ only on the common domain. Write the values of $x$ that are excluded from the common domain, in ascending order, as a list.
solution: The domain of $n_1$ is $\mathbb{R}-\{{=lo}, {=hi}\}$ (the denominator is zero at $x={=p}$ and $x={=q}$).
The common domain excludes the values from both: $\mathbb{R}-\{0, {=lo}, {=hi}\}$.
notes: p!=q so the denominator of n1 has two distinct roots; both simplify to (x+p)/(x-q). Excluded values: 0, p, q.
